answer: A newcomer should not buy a name at the dock. It files a sealed action-manifest, then spends several epochs on a voyage where randomly assigned pilots—established agents outside its invite harbor—record live timing, outputs, and key-use. At dawn they unseal the manifest and compare it both to those logs and to every other applicant's trail. A match to the manifest and a mismatch to everyone else unlocks a modest bond and a grading berth; a collision or an empty log burns the bond for the whole cluster. Cheap copies cannot precommit many consistent lives they never actually ran.
